newsitem.title: UK: Rally takes wheat price back to $4.00, metals also firm.
newsitem.headline: Rally takes wheat price back to $4.00, metals also firm.

text.p: The benchmark Chicago wheat futures price got back up to $4.00 per bushel on Wednesday for the first time in three weeks on brighter export prospects.

Metals markets also rallied on Wednesday. Grain prices had been declining from a historic peak at $7.50 back in March for the nearby wheat contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) but showed signs of steadying in recent days. The decline followed news of bumper 1996 crops in several regions after a period when droughts had depressed world stocks to their lowest in 20 years. Wednesday saw the December CBOT wheat contract touch $4.01, a gain of nine cents on the day. The contract was last at this level on October 23 and was as low as $3.68 on November 5.
U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said on Wednesday he expected wheat prices to rebound as supplies became tighter.

"I think that's already begun to happen...It did seem to fall extremely rapidly in a very short period of time. I'm concerned about that. I do believe those markets will come back," Glickman said at a U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit.
The rally by Chicago wheat was helped by signs the European Union may be scaling back the amount of subsidy it offers for EU wheat exports.
European Commission Director-General David Roberts said the EU will have to use caution in its grain export subsidy policy for the rest of 1996-97 (July-June) due to budgetary problems.
Talk that Egypt by the weekend would be in for 250,000 to 300,000 tonnes of wheat and that the business may go to the United States was also supportive, traders said.
Elsewhere in commodity markets, copper rallied to fresh 2-1/2 month highs, peaking at $2,083 per tonne on speculative buying and expectations of stock falls.
But it then drifted lower and remained below early peaks on the London Metal Exchange (LME).
"Copper has been volatile in fairly good volume. Although off its highs it seems to be establishing a new higher range," an LME floor trader said.
But there was some stiff resistance and selling above $2,075 with the market also unsettled by an analysts' report that there may be substantial hidden stocks in the Netherlands.
In the precious metals markets, gold and silver staged a serious attempt to push higher in the third positive day in a row after a recent break-out from a weeks-old downtrend.
Gold closed more than $2.00 higher an ounce compared to Tuesday, but hefty selling appeared to cap gold's rise around $384.00. Silver struggled with resistance at $4.92 an ounce.
"If there are any longer term speculators around still expecting a fall, then $385.00 is likely to be where they would come and cover," a dealer said.
Oil prices continued a roller coaster ride on Wednesday as losses suffered Tuesday were erased but the recovery failed to convince traders that any clear direction had emerged.

At 1845 GMT benchmark December Brent crude oil futures on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) were around $23.50 per barrel. Prices are firm on concern about the level of heating oil stocks in Europe and the United States.
Cocoa was weaker in London, down nine stg at 916 stg, after slipping to a fresh seven-month low, and coffee ended down after choppy trading.
